name: Santiago (Chile)
description: A vertical bicolour of blue at the hoist and yellow at the fly, charged at the centre with the arms of Santiago: a lion holding a sword on a silver field, within a border of eight gold scallops.
history: The flag of the commune of Santiago, the historic centre of the capital, bears the arms granted by Charles V on 12 February 1552 — a lion with a sword and eight scallops for Saint James. It is the commune's flag, distinct from that of the Metropolitan Region; no adoption date has been published.

features.role: arms of Santiago granted by Charles V on 12 February 1552
